rules.banned_because: Someone else's names, kept out of everything Euphonia publishes (Appendix E; setting/ip-review.md).
rules.fey_type_because: "Fey" survives only as the creature type; the setting's prose says "fae" (Book Two, What's Different). The 2024 rules' own names keep it too: Fey Ancestry, Fey Touched, Fey Wanderer, Summon Fey and the SRD's Conjure Fey (Chat, 15 November). So does a list of creature types: "any Undead, Fey, or Elemental".
rules.renames_because: The setting's own names for those planes, the first two of the Revelator's Cosmography: the Feywild is the Hidden, the Shadowfell the Ghostlands (setting/whats-out.md, wheel-and-plenum.md). The SRD's "the Feywild" reads "the Hidden".

regions.intro: The setting's own people here: where a party meets them, what they want and how a table uses them. The cast of the Great Game and the Venice Job comes first. Each has a pregen sheet except Máhte Ingá, Dorka Lakatos, Zofia Lipska and Don Gaspar de Rojas. The sheets are on the site, perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia.

people.name: Ser Marin Zorzi
people.text: One of Venice's three State Inquisitors, a tiefling of an old patrician house who has worn a plain white mask in court since his horns came in. You meet him only in the Ten's windowless court room, or by posting a denunciation in a lion's mouth: he reads them himself at night and can tell spite from fear by the handwriting. He wants to see the face of the halfling whose file he has read more often than his breviary. The Venice Job's villain, or its most dangerous patron; the brass figure at his elbow turns its head when you lie.

people.name: Zanetta Bon
people.text: A halfling carnival masker of the Giudecca who forged health passes, went into the Hidden and came home able to fold space. In Carnival she sits masked in a bauta at the Ridotto's faro table, losing small sums to a sergeant of the Ten's men. She wants her own file out of the Ten's archive, to read what they think she is. The Venice Job's way in and its way out, and the Crossing Danae on Venice's rooftops; what she owes the Hidden for the doors, she keeps to herself.

people.name: Simon Horowitz
people.text: The ghetto's Kabbalist, reading a book the angel Raziel gave him, a page at a time. The Venice Job's way into the ghetto, its reader of the scryers' hand and the one who knows the golem's word. His full entry is in Running Euphonia, Notable People.

people.name: Don Gaspar de Rojas
people.text: A canon of Toledo's cathedral and keeper of the chapter's archive, who holds the list of keys to the vaults under the city and has never been told what lies at the bottom of the deepest one. He works in the archive off the cloister from the morning office to noon, and walks the Zocodover in the evening, where every court's agent in Toledo has tried to buy him a drink. Since the winter the Archbishop's guards have taken a lantern down past his last door every Friday, and he wants to know why; he is a scholar, and not knowing is the one thing he can't bear. The Great Game's way into Toledo, or the man a rival court tries to buy.

people.name: Zofia Lipska
people.text: A deputy to the Sejm from the Sandomierz gentry, who has ended one session with a single word of protest and knows what that word is worth. The king abdicates in September, and the election that follows is open to every foreign purse: the agents of a French prince, a Neuburg and a Lorrainer have each offered to pay her debts. She lodges at an inn near Warsaw's castle when the Sejm sits, and has taken nobody's money yet. One of the three offers came with a spell on it, and she will hire a party to find out which before she votes. A patron for a Great Game in the east.

people.name: Matthias Kessler
people.text: A taster and apothecary's man at the Habsburg court in Vienna, paid to keep his masters alive, and by some of them for the other thing. He works the kitchens under the Hofburg at the dinner hour, and witnesses afterward can't describe his face. A Hollowed Counsellor, a poisoner who computes and feels nothing, he wants to keep the one thing he kept from before, and to keep anyone from knowing what it is. A villain or a contact for a Great Game in Vienna; agree at the table how much poisoning and coldness is shown before he appears.

people.name: Gennaro Esposito
people.text: Majordomo to a Neapolitan family, a foundling with the foundlings' surname, who keeps the books, hires the crews and decides who knows what, from a back room above a chandler's shop. He wants to stay the one person the family can't do without, and keeps three ledgers to manage it, one of them true. A patron who hires a party and already knows what it knows.

people.name: Fra Bertrand de Montclar
people.text: A gold-scaled dragonborn knight of the Order of St John, a younger son of the Langue of Provence, holding Candia's breaches in the siege's last full year. After dark he loses at dice to Venetian sappers in a casemate on the Sant'Andrea bastion, and confesses it on Saturdays. In the breach his sword lights like a church window and the men beside him can't be afraid. An ally or patron for anyone who wants something out of Candia before it falls.

people.name: Ilyanor Sael
people.text: Lanternhall's elf, Attending Physician and Chair of Vital Studies (see Running Euphonia, Notable People). He is on rounds on the Long Ward at the sixth bell, or in his office above the Library of Cases at any hour; he doesn't leave the Hall. He wants his graduates licensed in the countries they go home to: a patron for any Physician party and a problem for every licensing office in Europe.

people.name: Sister Ondine
people.text: The senior night sister on Lanternhall's Long Ward, who can't cast a spell and is the one person in the Hall every Physician obeys. She has threatened Ilyanor Sael with a blanket, and wants to see him sleep in a bed, once, with his eyes shut. She knows which patients will die by the way they ask for water. The ward's conscience and its comedy, and the one who sends an exhausted student to bed.

people.name: Anselme Lafrenaye
people.text: The graying halfling Gamester of the French court, with his own chair at the end of the lansquenet table at the king's high play, at Saint-Germain most weeks. He knows what Pascal and Fermat wrote to each other about dice, and generals who won't be seen asking a card player the odds lose to him first. A Counsellor's patron, rival or model; what he wants is in Running Euphonia, Notable People.

people.name: Kit Harrow
people.text: The Sharper of the pair called the Sharper and the Wit: a Cavalier baronet's daughter who plays hazard at the Groom Porter's in winter and the card rooms of Tunbridge Wells in August. She wants her father's estate back or, failing that, to be owed more than anyone in England. A player character as written, an ally or a rival (full entry in Running Euphonia, Notable People).

people.name: Ned Ashcombe
people.text: The Wit: Kit Harrow's husband, a Royalist colonel's younger son whose lampoons all London sings and whose couplets are signals to her across the room. He wants the place at court the Restoration promised his father's son, on terms that don't cost him Kit. A player character as written, an ally or a rival.

people.name: Étaín of the Ford
people.text: A wild elf of the Bordermarches, the shifting country where the Hidden Realm and the world overlap, who has ridden with the Wild Hunt since before the parish churches were built. A village meets her at the ford below it on the first dark night after Samhain, hounds ahead of her, her body turned in its skin by the ríastrad. She has never been able to throw away a child's wooden horse from a raid three hundred years ago, and wants to know whose it was. A villain for a game on the Border, or a foil someone patient could talk to in the light half.

people.name: Morfudd Prys
people.text: A dwarf of the old mines on the Welsh border who keeps the gate against the Hidden for her village, walking the boundary at dusk through the dark half with a mastiff, an iron bell and her buff coat worn inside out. She wants to find the last Killer, her parent, taken on a Samhain night when she was twelve. An ally or teacher on the Border; the new magistrate thinks she's a cunning woman and would like to see her license.

people.name: Tadhg Ó Laoi
people.text: A Connacht fiddler of Queen Elizabeth's time who played one night under the hill and came home a century late, to the Ireland of the transplantation. Hear him at a wedding, or in a shebeen on a fair night where an old woman has started to cry at a tune nobody alive should know. He wants to learn what he owes the Hidden before they come to collect it. An ally and a contact, with a purse of harp shillings no one will take.

people.name: Neeltje Claesdochter
people.text: Leiden's ice-reader, who walks the frozen canals at dawn with a pole, an auger and a hedge charm her mother taught her, and says which ice will bear; the city licenses her through the fishmongers' guild. She runs her own *koek-en-zopie* stall on the Rhine, can't read and has never been wrong about ice. She wants her granddaughter to have the license before the guild gives it to a man with a book.

people.name: Piero Neri
people.text: A wool-carder of Santo Spirito and a captain of the Misericordia, who has carried Florence's sick to the hospital under a black hood for nineteen years. The man to ask who in Florence is sick, poor, dying or newly arrived, and the brother who wants the lute taken home (see Life Here).

people.name: Brites Fagundes
people.text: A halfling baker of the Alfama, Lisbon's old quarter, whose bread is as good on the third day as the first; a sailor from Sofala paid a debt with the Mutapan Cold Box in her back room, and she has never asked what it's worth. She wants someone to stop the Holy Office's familiar who has started buying a loaf every day and taking it away uneaten. A host, a safe kitchen and a quiet thread to Mutapa.

people.name: Máhte Ingá
people.text: A noaidi of the Lule Sámi: Ingá, Máhtte's daughter, who reads the drum for three *siidas*, the herding communities of her district. A party meets her at the winter market at Jokkmokk, where the crown's bailiff takes the tax and the priest counts who came to church. A priest took her uncle's drum to a cabinet in Stockholm, and she will read the drum for a party's road in exchange for word of where it is now. A guide and an ally in the north; to the hunts, what she does is unlicensed magic.

people.name: Dorka Lakatos
people.text: A Romani nail-smith in the quarter outside the walls of Hermannstadt, in Transylvania, whose family forge works under the town's letter of protection. She makes the nails the Saxon villages drive into their gateposts for the dark half, and the same villages name her people when a child goes missing. She keeps a count of which villages bought no iron this year, and needs someone a magistrate will listen to, to carry it before the autumn open night. The source of iron for any Border game east of Vienna.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here, the Great Game's and the Monsoon Road's cast first. Each has a pregen sheet. The sheets are on the site, perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia.

people.name: Simbarashe Moyo
people.text: Mutapa's great artificer, about eighty, in his workshop in Sofala's old town with an iron construct at the door. A mentor or patron, and the man whose choice a party can force. His full entry is in Running Euphonia, Notable People.

people.name: Shiri
people.text: Mutapa's spymaster, who runs the foreign service from one room above the House of the Bird. A party meets her factor in Sofala or Hoerikwaggo and gets its orders under a soapstone-bird seal. A patron who pays on time, every time. Her full entry is in Running Euphonia, Notable People.

people.name: Munyaradzi Shava
people.text: Master of the Shava house, the merchant house that carries the king's shewstones abroad and now stands half a step behind the king's left shoulder. He keeps a counting room in Sofala's new quarter and a place at court, where he listens without blinking; it was his men who went to the great artificer's workshop at night. A lowland fever took his father and both his brothers when he was twenty-two and left him the house. He remembers loving them the way you remember a country you once visited, and keeps their three stools against the counting-room wall, where nobody else may sit. He wants a shewstone in every court on earth before the mediums or the old man can stop it, and the house safe for his daughter Rufaro, who is nine. The Great Game's villain on Mutapa's side, or its best-paying patron.

people.name: Dona Catarina de Sá
people.text: An Afro-Portuguese prazo heiress who lost her land below Tete when Mutapa kept its mines, and now runs the platinum runners of Sofala. She spends the hottest hour at a cook-shop by the fish market, shelling prawns and asking after your family by name, though she has never met them. Nobody caught with platinum in Sofala can say where it came from, because she makes sure they never knew, and she pays her runners' widows. A villain or contact on the Monsoon Road; a Lisbon lawyer says a European court might honor her deed, and she hasn't decided whether she wants it back.

people.name: Rashid bin Khamis al-Ghafiri
people.text: A Muscat dhow captain with the storm in his blood, an air elemental-blood (descended from an elemental that took a human shape and forgot) on his mother's side, who learned to tie winds into cord from her father on the Batinah coast. When the northeast monsoon brings the dhows in, he works every quay from Pate to Kilwa, selling fair winds by the knot to captains who swear they don't need them. A knot is a length of cord he has tied a wind into; untied aboard, it gives the ship a fair wind until he next sleeps. He wants to keep carrying dates and Gulf horses instead of guns for as long as the imam, Sultan bin Saif, lets him, and the imam's officers have started asking about his hold. A patron or rival on the Monsoon Road.

people.name: Mwalimu Bakari Shee
people.text: A Bajuni pilot of Faza, a water elemental-blood, like his grandmother, who went over the side in a squall at fourteen and came up three days later a mile out, breathing easily, with a promise to someone in the deep that he still keeps. Find him sitting on an upturned hull on the beach at Faza or the Lamu waterfront when a captain needs a pilot for deep water. He knows which waters take a toll, leaves a gift over certain soundings without explaining, and wants to be released from the promise, which he has never dared ask. An ally or contact; his pact is a Dreamlord's, with something in the deep.

people.name: Tonderai Shumba
people.text: The king's lion at Sofala's outermost gate, a Lionskin Guardian in a lion-helmed suit with a copper-wire mane. At dawn, when the merchant houses' carters line up to argue the fee, he agrees warmly that the road is theirs and keeps the gate shut. He has been posted to four gates without changing jobs, because the city keeps moving its edge outward, and wants one that stays put a whole season. An ally or a foil, and Sofala's new border in one man.

people.name: Tsitsi
people.text: The go-between at Hoerikwaggo, a Khoekhoe woman of twenty-five raised in the harbor town. Find her on the harbor steps when a ship comes in, translating for everyone at once, every word exact except, now and then, one. The town calls her Tsitsi, Shona for mercy; her own name she keeps to herself, and what she wants is her people's grazing, cattle and terms kept, whatever flag is in the bay. A contact or ally, owned by none of the parties who think they own her. In our history the go-between at the Cape was Krotoa, who lost her husband in 1668 and her place the year after.

people.name: Ambuya Rudo Gumbo
people.text: The senior royal medium, through whom a king two centuries dead speaks on rain and war, and who has lately said things about the shewstones the living king didn't want to hear. A party meets her at court on the day the royal spirit is asked a question, or at home the next day shelling groundnuts, cross about it; she remembers nothing of what he says. She wants to be spoken to for an afternoon as herself. A patron or ally on the mediums' side of the question of who governs.

people.name: Nyarai Soko
people.text: Master of the Mhizha Guild, who swept the great artificer's floor at fourteen and wrote down how he did things so that others could, which he has never quite forgiven. Find her at the guild hall in Sofala on entry day, reading each new journeyman's name aloud twice. She wants the guild's method written down so completely that it no longer needs Simbarashe, and she wants him to say she was right. A patron or foil, whose stamp is on every piece the guild sells.

people.name: Fadzai Shoko
people.text: One of Mutapa's two healers at Hoerikwaggo, a Vitalist who treats the town under the mountain as one patient and the mountain as part of it, from a fever house on the slope with every shutter open at noon. When the sickness comes there will be more patients than she can reach, and she wants to talk over whom to treat first with someone who doesn't work for anyone. An ally or contact for the ship with the fever (see Hooks).

people.name: Tapiwa Marufu
people.text: An mbira player who plays every bira in Sofala's new quarter from dusk to dawn, and by day tunes the guild's singing birds to mbira songs the guild says it never taught him. He has a welcome in every household in the quarter and hears what each one is praying for. He wants to know who taught the birds his songs, since nobody living did.

people.name: Amai Rutendo Chigumba
people.text: Keeper of the king's granary at Sofala, who decides who eats from it and has never once asked anyone's business. At dusk she stands at the granary door with a ladle and a pot of sadza; half the guild's journeymen ate from her pot in their first month in the city, and they still bring her the first of their wages. She wants the new granary's walls up before the rains and the sickness, and puts anyone who offers to help on the end of a hod. The best-loved person in Sofala.

regions.region: The Ottomans, Persia and the Horn
regions.intro: The setting's own people here. The Isfahan entries come first (Farrokh, Golnar, Shushan Ghukasian, Khodadad, Khadijeh Khatun and Abbas-qoli): they are one cast and can be run as one adventure. Each has a pregen sheet. The sheets are on the site, perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia.

people.name: Farrokh of Isfahan
people.text: The pari-touched elf (see The Hidden Here), who went to a pari wedding at Nowruz, ate at the feast and came back three years later in the wedding robe, green silk gone sea-gray at the hems. After the evening prayer he sits in the corner of a coffeehouse off the Maidan, letting a water pipe bubble that he doesn't inhale. He wants the way back in and can't leave it alone. He can tell by looking who else has been to the wedding and come back, so the families of the taken find him: an ally or contact for the pari wedding (see Hooks).

people.name: Golnar
people.text: A pari of the bride's family at the wedding Farrokh ran from, holding a shape in Isfahan to get the painted glass cup back, and remembering every minute of what she is. She sits by a fountain on the Maidan at dusk, in a green nobody else seems to notice; when she sits at your table, every water flask you carry is suddenly full of rosewater. She wants the cup back unbroken and Farrokh returned to the feast of his own free will, which she thinks kinder than the other way, and she knows where Shushan Ghukasian's son is and won't say. A villain or foil, polite, patient and bound by every promise she makes.

people.name: Shushan Ghukasian
people.text: The widowed head of a New Julfa silk house with partners in Surat, Venice and Amsterdam, who hires crews for the Bandar Abbas and Surat run and pays in credit good from Amsterdam to Manila. Find her in her counting room off the Vank cathedral square, reading a bill of exchange, a manifest and your faces in that order. Her younger son went to a pari wedding at Nowruz with a flute and hasn't come back; she has paid a priest, a dervish and an astrologer, and decided it's time for people who carry swords. The patron of the pari wedding (see Hooks), and a Monsoon Road employer after.

people.name: Khodadad the Dyer
people.text: The Zoroastrian dyer who was set on the throne before the second coronation to take the bad stars off the shah (see Magic Here); it worked, and as far as anyone can tell he still has them. He's knee-deep in a dye vat in Isfahan's Zoroastrian quarter, arms blue to the elbow, hoping you're a customer; when he hears who sent you, he sits down in the dye. He wants to be forgotten, or failing that, for his daughter's wedding to go ahead with nothing going wrong at it. The heart of the substitute (see Hooks): one court faction wants him safe and quiet, another wants him back on the throne for an afternoon.

people.name: Khadijeh Khatun
people.text: Stewardess of the shah's mother's household, called the Key, who decides which letters, petitions and rumors go in to the women who decide what reaches the shah. Meet her in a garden pavilion of the royal harem, through a screen, with sherbet already poured for the number of visitors she was told to expect. She has someone in every great house in Isfahan, usually a cook, and wants her nephew placed in the chancery and her own name kept out of every European's travel book. A patron or rival for a Great Game at Isfahan.

people.name: Abbas-qoli the Teller
people.text: A naqqal of Isfahan, who tells the *Shahnameh* in a coffeehouse off the Maidan with a stick for a sword and can make a room of grown men cry over Sohrab. After the evening prayer he is on his stool, two tables from Farrokh of Isfahan, collecting coppers in a cloth cap and refusing to say what happens tomorrow. His daughter Parvaneh tells it better than he does, to the women of the quarter on the roofs on summer nights, and what he wants is one hall where they can both tell it. A contact who hears everything a coffeehouse says, and the best way to spend an evening in Isfahan.

people.name: Mustafa Remzi Efendi
people.text: He picks the hour at which the sultan acts. The chief astrologer, the *müneccimbaşı*, is the empire's minister of magic; the new chief is Ahmed Dede, and Remzi, the senior astrologer under him, does the measuring, on a terrace of the Topkapı an hour before dawn, astrolabe at arm's length, while the court waits in the cold for his finger to lift. The Kadızadeli preachers want him gone and the Köprülü viziers need him; he wants to be left alone long enough to finish tables the Frankish astronomers will have to copy. A patron or mentor, with a Mutapan device in parts on his table.

people.name: Yusuf Rais
people.text: A captain of the *taifa*, Algiers' corsair captains' guild, born Tom Penhale of Falmouth. Meet him at the taifa's counting house by the mole, pricing every name on a ransom list in three currencies without looking up. He takes ships, ransoms what he takes and buys Muslim captives back out of Malta and Livorno, and wants both sets of books balanced, the guild's and his own, with nobody reading the second. A patron or rival for any ransom job (see Hooks).

people.name: Wäldä Mika'el
people.text: A *däbtära* of Gondar, an unordained church scholar, cantor and poet who writes God's secret names on healing scrolls for Christian, Muslim and Beta Israel clients alike; he turns up in any courtyard where a child is sick. He wants to go to Enfraz and argue with Zera Yacob, the old scholar there who tests every religion by reason. An ally or teacher, and a good friend to have when a *buda* charge is made.

people.name: Hafız Ömer
people.text: A young Kadızadeli preacher in Istanbul, honest, learned and certain that the lodges, the coffee and the talisman-makers are innovations the Prophet never knew. His prayers are answered, and so are the dervishes', which he doesn't discuss; he would close the lodges and carry a dervish's shopping home on the way. He wants the lodges shut by law before his followers shut them with torches. A foil or rival.

people.name: Nafisa al-Qalyubiyya
people.text: A physician of al-Mansuri, the Cairo hospital that has taught at the bedside for nearly four hundred years, who runs its plague service and finds Lanternhall's fame puzzling. She noticed in 1651 what Lanternhall noticed, that a patient cured by magic catches the same fever again, and wants her notes read by someone in Basel who will take them seriously. A mentor or contact for any Physician.

people.name: Nane Gulbahar
people.text: A Tabriz midwife who keeps the forty days after a birth against the Āl, and has never lost a mother to her. She sits through the night across a new mother's doorway, an iron sickle on her knees; when something thin with a clay nose looks round the gate, she says its name without getting up. She wants an apprentice with younger knees who isn't afraid of the dark. A mentor or ally, and a Hidden Killer by another name.

people.name: Saliha Hatun
people.text: A widow of Üsküdar who left her husband's fortune to a waqf that dresses poor brides and keeps her street's fountain cold in summer. She receives after the afternoon prayer behind a screen, with the waqf's deed on a cushion beside her. Her nephew, the trustee, has started to borrow from it (the trousseau, under Life Here's Hooks).

people.name: Wälättä Śellase
people.text: A widow of Gondar whose tej is the best in the city, and who hosts the mahbär of St Mary on the twenty-first of each month, with priests, masons and a däbtära arguing on one bench. She knows what every household in her quarter is short of, and which of her neighbors the council's decree is about to move. A host, and the person to ask before you try to help anyone in Gondar.

people.name: Ferhad Usta
people.text: An elf of Istanbul, second master of the confectionery in the Topkapı's kitchens, whose grandmother, the family says, was a pari. His violet sherbet is cooled with Uludağ snow, and three viziers' cooks have failed to copy his *zülbiye* helva. He wants the next Feast of the Sacrifice's helva to be the best the sultan has ever tasted, and has started to dream of a sweeter table than this world sets, which frightens him. A patron with the palace's ear.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here. Each has a pregen sheet. The sheets are on the site, perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia.

people.name: Akinwale
people.text: A front-rank horseman of Oyo's cavalry who is ridden by his orisha in battle and remembers none of it. In the dry season he is in the horse lines outside Oyo Ile, rubbing down a Nupe war-horse that cost more than his house; he looks at your horse's eyes before he looks at yours. He wants that horse alive through one more rainy season, and to hear from someone who saw it what he was laughing at in the ford. An ally or contact.

people.name: Dom Garcia Nsaku
people.text: A Soyo shield-bearer who carries Count Paulo da Silva's letters to people who would rather not receive them, and comes back. He hears Mass from the Capuchins and stops at the nganga's door on the way home to ask after the count's oath-bundle, and sees no contradiction. He wants to learn whether Soyo means to reunite Kongo, rule it or keep it broken before he is asked to fight for the answer. An ally or patron, and Soyo's man on the road if Count Paulo sends to Sofala.

people.name: Olaniyi
people.text: Master of the Alaafin's horse, sworn into the Ogboni, who knows to the animal how many mounts Oyo has, how many it can buy from Nupe and how many the forest will kill; before the dry-season campaign he lives in the royal stables at Oyo Ile, a tally-stick in each hand. He is the patron of the horse (see Hooks), and would forgive the one who can do it almost anything.

people.name: Ayoka
people.text: A chanter of *oríkì*, the praise poetry of Oyo's families, who knows every lineage's glories and the parts it leaves out. She greets a stranger with a line of praise for their grandfather, made up on the spot, and trades what she knows for a story she hasn't heard. She wants the oríkì of a family nobody in Oyo has heard of, and to be the first to chant it.

people.name: Buatu Makaya
people.text: A Vili merchant of Loango who carries copper and cloth to Malebo Pool and speaks the language of every valley on the road, including some no one taught him. One of the languages he dreams in belongs to no valley he has found, and he wants to find it. A contact, and the best guide on the copper road for a party that wants to arrive with its manners intact.

people.name: Ndona Nsimba
people.text: A nganga of Soyo who heals, divines, guards against the ndoki and makes the oath minkisi that seal the count's treaties, at her compound on the edge of the sacred wood of Nfinda Ngula. She and the Capuchin heal the same fevers in the same streets under an arrangement neither admits to, and she wants him to stop burning her work and start asking what it's for. An ally or teacher; lords who break an oath sworn on one of her bundles have been known to sicken.

people.name: Dona Leonor Mvemba
people.text: A Kongo noblewoman widowed at Mbwila, who swore over her husband's body to bring the king's crown and scepter home from Lisbon, and the oath took. She receives visitors in a borrowed house in Mbanza Soyo, in her late husband's best cloak, as if the kingdom were still whole. The patron of the crown in Lisbon (see Hooks), honest that what her house does with the crown afterward is her house's business.

people.name: Osaretin
people.text: A master of the oba's guild of brass-casters in Benin City, who casts the court's history in metal and can read a room's ranks from where people stand. He has heard that Europe's ministers of magic are reading about Benin's palace in Dapper's new book, and wants to see it and find out what the Dutch got wrong. A contact at the oba's court, and a reason to carry a book from Amsterdam.

people.name: Akosua Nyarko
people.text: An Akan hunter who walks the forest's edge behind Accra for her village, keeps the owners' rules and deals with what doesn't. She has met the mmoatia three times and wants to learn what they teach the priests without paying the priests' price. An ally or guide for a game on the Border, for a fair fee and the promise that you'll do exactly as she says at the shrines.

people.name: Alfa Mahmud Gurdu
people.text: Keeper of a Timbuktu family library near the Sankore mosque, and a master of the science of letters, who corrects a student's grammar without opening his eyes. His grandfather walled up a room when the Moroccans carried the scholars away, the family is still unwalling it shelf by shelf, and he wants a copyist with a steady hand and a good memory. A mentor or patron who pays in knowledge, which he considers the more generous currency.

people.name: Sossi
people.text: A market woman of Allada who has sold everything she can sell and walked to the beach at Offra to buy her brother back before the company ship sails. She sits by a company lodge counting cowries on a mat, in her best cloth, never once looking at the ship. The patron of the roads at Offra (see Hooks), who will owe a party for the rest of her life and pay it.

people.name: Iya Adunni
people.text: The mother of the palace market at Oyo Ile, who settles every quarrel in it before sundown from a stool where the cloth row crosses the pepper row. The palace doesn't overturn her verdicts. She wants a Mutapan singing bird for the night market, one of the kind that sings when a hand goes into the wrong basket, and will trade a great deal of what she knows for it.

people.name: Ndona Mvita
people.text: A palm-wine seller of Mbanza Soyo, whose bench under the plaza's great tree is the one place in the province where the Capuchin, the nganga, the Dutch factor and the count's shield-bearers drink together; she repeats nothing she hears. Her son is a mestre who teaches the faith in the villages, and she wants him ordained a priest, which the bishop in Luanda won't do for a Kongolese. A peacemaker, and the person who knows who is quarreling with whom.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here. Each has a pregen sheet. The sheets are on the site, perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia.

people.name: Kesavan Vaidyan
people.text: A Malabar surgeon whose family craft is the nose rebuilt from the patient's own skin, and whose knife floats while his hands stay folded in his lap. Patients from both sides of the nose-cutting wars between Mysore and Madurai pass each other on his road without speaking; he charges the poor in rice and the poligars in gold, and gives both the same attention. He wants to see a nose he rebuilt twenty years ago and know that it held. A mentor or ally for any Physician.

people.name: Amritnath
people.text: A Nath yogi who has stopped aging and no longer needs food, water or air, and takes all three out of courtesy. At dawn he sits at his *dhuni* on the pilgrim road above the Ganges plain, and lets the raja's men who come to ask how to live forever wait until noon. He gives the old inoculation against smallpox to anyone who sits still, and wants the last *siddhi*, the deathless body. A mentor, or a foil to Lanternhall's Ilyanor Sael, who stopped reaching for the same thing.

people.name: Manekbai Parekh
people.text: A Jain shroff's widow who runs her late husband's banking house in Surat and writes hundis honored from Mocha to Malacca, doing sums aloud in Gujarati faster than the English president's writer can on paper. She'll stake a party's voyage at a rate that depends on how much she likes them, and she likes very few; she wants her grandson to take the house before her husband's brothers do. A Monsoon Road patron.

people.name: Kunhi Ayesha
people.text: A Mappila pepper broker on the Calicut beach, who sells the Zamorin's officers news of every ship and every ship news of the Zamorin's officers. She can repeat word for word what a Dutch captain said three tables away. A contact, at a price she names after she has heard why you ask.

people.name: Abdul Wahid
people.text: The Surat muhtasib's clerk, who reads every foreigner's permit to practice magic and checks whether the official who signed it is still in office. He is honest, pious, underpaid and very good at his job, and wants to be the first clerk in Surat to read the emperor's new law book and find that it agrees with him. A foil for a permit nobody will name (see Hooks), and the worst man a smuggler can meet.

people.name: Rakhmabai Deshmukh
people.text: A Maratha deshmukh's widow who took the fort's keys from her husband's belt before the funeral and holds his hill fort in the Western Ghats for Shivaji. Find her on the gate bastion at dusk, counting the Mughal patrol fires on the plain, or at a truce table, winning. She wants the peace with the viceroy to last one more monsoon, until the cistern is cut and the granary full. A patron or rival, who plays chess with the enemy and wins in the margins.

people.name: Kunwar Ratan Singh
people.text: A younger prince of a minor Hada Rajput house, serving in the Mughal army of the Deccan at Aurangabad, who fences like water and has never lost his temper in public. Rakhmabai Deshmukh has beaten him at chess twice across a truce table and he would like a third game; what he wants most is land of his own rather than his elder brother's. A rival, a love interest or a gracious enemy.

people.name: Ammakka
people.text: A dwarf diamond appraiser of Golconda, of a family that says it came from the treasure-keeping yakshas, who is testing whether a diamond can do for magic what platinum does for Mutapa. Her trials so far are inconclusive and twice explosive, the notebook lives in a pot of rice, and she wants a clean answer with nobody from three crowns watching. A contact or patron for the untested stone (see Hooks).

people.name: Ponni
people.text: A potter-priest's daughter of seventeen near Madurai, who helps make Ayyanar's terracotta horses and has started riding out behind them at the boundary on dark-half nights, with a sickle and a clay lamp. She has better hands for clay than either brother, and wants her father to let her make one horse that is hers alone. Quietly furious about almost everything, and a Hidden Killer just starting out.

people.name: Saadat Ali
people.text: A singer of the imperial court at Delhi, out of work since the emperor stopped hearing music. He sings every night in a walled garden outside the Ajmeri Gate for a patron behind a screen who pays in gold of a reign nobody can name, and comes home at dawn thinner each week. He wants to be asked back. The singer of the garden (see Hooks).

people.name: Perundevi
people.text: Keeper of the chatram her mother endowed on the Alagar road outside Madurai, who has cooked for every Chithirai festival since she was nine. The village that owes the chatram its rice hasn't paid since Mysore's war, and she means to feed the festival anyway. The patron of the rice for the road (see Life Here).

people.name: Mai Raji
people.text: The cook of the langar at the Sikh sangat in Dhaka, who has fed Mughal soldiers, Bengali boatmen, Portuguese deserters and an Armenian merchant at one sitting, in one line, and sets whoever is nearest to wash the pots. She wants news of the ninth Guru's party on the road to Assam, where her nephew rides as a cook, and whoever brings it eats free for a month. A host, and the safest table in Bengal.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here. Lu Qingxu, Gu Wenyuan, Shen Xuanji and Hu Lanxin, first, are the cast of the Tomb Road, the tomb-robbing game in Adventures and Hooks. Each has a pregen sheet except Nang Bua. The sheets are on the site, perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia.

people.name: Lu Qingxu
people.text: The last of a line of Ming court alchemists, one of the Qiu Xian Zhe (see Powers and Factions, Seekers of Immortality), in Daoist dress that keeps the queue off his head and the questions off his past. Find him at a hill hermitage with a luopan on the table and the Bureau's old sealing calendar open beside it, or at the last door of a tomb by lamplight. He carries a red pill from the batch his teacher died of, and wants to learn whether the batch was wrong, or the teacher. An ally or mentor who digs where the sealing dates don't add up: the Tomb Road's fallen alchemist.

people.name: Gu Wenyuan
people.text: A dragonborn calendar clerk of Yang Guangxian's Astronomical Bureau, who will be out of work the day the shadow falls the Jesuits' way and has found a Ming prince's sealing date that doesn't add up. At night he is at the observatory on the city wall, or in a teahouse nearby doing long division on a tea bill with his sleeve pulled down over the scales on his wrist. He wants to prove the arithmetic wrong before anyone burns the records, mostly so someone will know he was right. The clerk (see Hooks) who opens the Tomb Road: a patron or a fellow delver.

people.name: Shen Xuanji
people.text: A fallen court alchemist, seventy-four and looking forty-five, who compounds mineral elixirs for rich men in Beijing. He sees visitors by introduction only, after dark, in the back room of a medicine shop near the Drum Tower that smells of mercury. His illusions are first-rate and his elixirs are mercury; he has decided Lu Qingxu's teacher found something real, and he wants to be young, actually. The Tomb Road's villain, always one tomb ahead.

people.name: Hu Lanxin
people.text: A fox spirit in a woman's shape who remembers what she is, and is after the same tomb the party is, for the fox-jade buried with a prince who once loved her. Meet her already inside a sealed Ming tomb when the party breaks through, sitting on the coffin eating their dried plums and asking what took them so long. She is honest about everything except her age, wants the jade back because it's hers, and wants to know whether he was buried holding it. A rival or love interest on the Tomb Road.

people.name: Shi Yuanjing
people.text: A Shaolin fighting monk the abbot sends down alone with a staff to meet whatever official comes up the valley road, because he is calm, polite and plainly impossible to arrest; he reached the gate tower's lintel on Mount Song by walking three steps up its face. His ordination certificate dates from the last Ming years, and no Qing clerk has asked to see it yet. He wants not to have to decide what he'll do when the governor tells the monks to stop drilling; until then, an ally or teacher.

people.name: Tachibana Chiyo
people.text: An aasimar shrine priestess in a mountain province of Japan, born with the light in her, who is sent for when a child is lost at dusk (see The Hidden Here). She wants the province to send a second priestess before a child is lost on a night when she is already out. An ally for a child hidden by the kami, or by something that isn't one.

people.name: Daeng Calla
people.text: A Makassarese halfling smuggler with a share in a padewakang, who moves Mutapan curiosities without a ministry stamp and carries letters out through the lines at Somba Opu, smiling at a Dutch boarding officer and telling him the long crate is rattan. Her lamps drift every month, and she wants someone with Mutapan training aboard. An ally or contact for the last sortie (see Hooks); her grandmother says the family came from the orang bunian, and she says that explains the hiding and nothing else.

people.name: Brother Joris Vanhove
people.text: A Flemish Jesuit lay brother in Beijing who can cast a cannon, mend a clock and compute a noon shadow, and is checking every figure he can before December. He likes the Bureau's Chinese astronomers better than the Portuguese fathers, thinks the gnomon trial the most honest test he'll ever see, and is terrified. A contact or ally for the witness (see Hooks).

people.name: Ok Rye-hwa
people.text: A Korean *mudang* outside Seoul's walls, who bargains with the spirits for her neighbors, pays the state's tax on shamans and is despised by the scholars who send for her at night. At a *gut* she dances barefoot on the blades of two fodder-choppers in a general's hat. She wants her daughter to inherit the drum and the clients without the contempt. An ally or contact for any game in Joseon.

people.name: Teungku Fatimah
people.text: A scholar of the science of letters at the court of Aceh's queen, Sultanah Safiatuddin, who writes the talismans on the port's walls and is one reason the Dutch knock before entering. She wants a book of letters she has only seen quoted, said to be in a Bohra library in Surat, and pays for books in pepper, generously. A Monsoon Road patron.

people.name: Nang Bua
people.text: A river pilot of Ayutthaya, who takes foreign ships from the bar up the Chao Phraya to the city in a narrow boat with a red awning, and tells each captain which of King Narai's ministers to visit first, and with what gift. The captains pay her, and so do two of the ministers and the Japanese quarter. She wants a boat of her own for her daughter before the ministers' quarrel sinks them all. The way into Narai's court for a party that arrives by sea.

people.name: Chea Sok
people.text: A Khmer former monk called by spirit illness at Angkor, who sees the temple as the world-mountain it was built to be and guides pilgrims through it by night, describing with complete calm the five peaks above the central tower that nobody else can see. He wants to know why the mountain answered a Japanese pilgrim who thought he was somewhere else. A mentor or contact for any game at Angkor (see Angkor).

people.name: Wang Yuezhen
people.text: A Suzhou *tanci* singer who has told the same love story in a teahouse by the Chang Gate every afternoon for eleven weeks, stopping each day on the best line. Everyone talks under the music, so she knows the city's business. A contact for anything in Suzhou, and the singer asked to stand in for the last song on Tiger Hill, if the fox allows it (see Life Here).

people.name: Panay
people.text: An Amis woman, the eldest sister of her house on Taiwan's east coast, who runs its fields, its rice and its marriages, and feeds whoever came along the coast that day. She wants Chengtian's soldiers kept on their own side of the mountains. A host and an ally, and the first open door on the east coast.

people.name: Đào Thị Lựu
people.text: The head of a water-puppet guild in a village outside Thang Long, the first woman to keep the guild's book and swear its oath, which forbids teaching the tricks to anyone who might marry out of the village. She taught them to her daughters anyway and dared the elders to say so. She wants her troupe to play for the Trịnh lord's court at New Year. A host, a contact and a way into court.

people.name: Kichibei
people.text: A tempura seller at the foot of Nihonbashi in Edo, a century before the city takes to the dish; his batter came from a Nagasaki cook who learned it in a Portuguese kitchen before the ban. Since spring he has been losing customers to a second stall across the bridge, whose fish is never out of season and whose owner nobody has seen in daylight, and he wants to know what is frying there. A source of every rumor on the Tōkaidō.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here, the High Ground's cast first. Each has a pregen sheet. The sheets are on the site, perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia.

people.name: Kusi Wallpa
people.text: The Sapa Inca's senior staff officer on the Apurímac front, who reads Spanish columns by their dust and empties the storehouses on their road before they arrive. Find him on a cold rock above a column's road, a khipu across his knees and a runner waiting. He hires outsiders for what a khipu can't do (reading a Spanish captain, buying a mule-driver, finding who in Potosí sells powder to both sides) and pays in cloth, safe roads and his word. The patron of an Inca start in The High Ground, who wants the Spanish column turned back before the harvest, with as few of his own counted out of the khipu as he can manage.

people.name: Waman Illa
people.text: A storm-priest of the high valleys above the Apurímac, struck by lightning as a boy herder, who keeps a huaca that rose in the Taki Onqoy years and speaks for it to the Sapa Inca's officers, and for them to it. Officers climb to his shelf above the Apurímac crossing with khipus of the Spanish column and leave with rain, and a list of what the huaca wants in return; he offers everyone coca while they decide whether to pay. He wants to see the war end before the huaca decides it likes it. A patron or ally for an Inca start in The High Ground (see Adventures and Hooks).

people.name: Willka Mamani
people.text: A Kallawaya healer of Charazani who walks the war's roads with close to a thousand plants in his head, treating Inca runners and Spanish muleteers alike. He walks the road between the lines with a mule and a woven bag of medicines, stopping wherever someone is sick. Both armies let him through because both need him, and he sells each exactly as much news of the other; he wants the road kept open to healers whoever wins, and has asked both commanders to swear it. A mentor, and the best guide across the line alive.

people.name: Licenciado Diego Ruiz de Lezcano
people.text: A visitor-general of idolatries for the Archbishop of Lima, who burns the mummified dead and the stones that speak, and whose prayers work, which he takes as proof. He sets up at a table in a highland plaza with a notary, soldiers and a bonfire laid but not yet lit, calling the village's ancestors by name in a gentle voice and writing down who doesn't answer. He is sincere, learned and kind to children, and wants one village where the stone stays silent after he has prayed over it. A villain for the visitations (see Trouble Brewing), and a frightened man.

people.name: Čhaŋté Wašté Wiŋ
people.text: A Dakota druid of the lake country around Mille Lacs who hunts bison on foot with her people and takes the bison's shape, a fact about her rather than a secret. She lets the young men tell her story wrong, and wants a good harvest, a quiet winter and no black-robed visitors; she has seen one Frenchman, at a distance, carrying a kettle, and has not felt the lack. An ally or mentor on her own ground, where she has enough to do.

people.name: Aj K'in Kuch
people.text: An Itza priest who reads the k'atun count for the Aj Kan Ek' at Nojpetén, and has seen, past the edge of the world, why it is not yet time; he tells a friar politely and precisely that he has come twenty-nine years too early. He wants the surveyor never to arrive, and the count kept by more than one reader in case he does. A patron or mentor for the survey (see Hooks).

people.name: Ganonhsese
people.text: An Onondaga Clan Mother, among the Firekeepers of the Haudenosaunee, who chooses her clan's chief for the Grand Council and can remove him. Find her in her longhouse at Onondaga in winter, shelling beans with her daughters while a council chief explains himself to her. The patron of the drumming (see Hooks), who pays in the Confederacy's remembering.

people.name: Kima Ismare
people.text: A Wounaan *jaibaná* of the upper San Juan, hired by her people to keep a river shut against the mining families from Popayán, who have hired another jaibaná to open it. She has kept it shut six years from under her stilt house, and wants to outlast her rival, a man she trained and is not proud of. A patron or foil for opening the river (see Hooks), paid in fish, cloth and the right to be cross with everyone.

people.name: Ana Kitumba
people.text: A captain of Palmares, born free behind the palisade at Macaco after her mother came up from a Pernambuco sugar mill with a baby and nothing else. At dusk she walks the palisade greeting every sentry by name; by day she sits at council in the king's house. She wants a child of hers to grow old in Palmares without having to fight for it. An ally or patron.

people.name: Brás Furtado
people.text: A *capitão-do-mato*, a hunter of people who escaped slavery, whom the sugar planters of Pernambuco hire to lead their expeditions against Palmares, naming the price per head without looking up. He has studied every expedition that failed against Palmares and knows why each did, which is why Ana Kitumba knows his name. A villain from a hard part of the record; a table chooses how much of him to use.

people.name: Doña Isabel Cuauhtzin
people.text: A Nahua cacica of a noble Xochimilco family who paints portrait miniatures for the viceroy's court in Mexico City, and so holds the likeness of everyone worth scrying in New Spain. She keeps her family's lawsuit over their Xochimilco lands going in Spanish, and has started, very quietly, painting her likenesses slightly wrong. A contact for a Great Game in New Spain; three services want her sketchbooks.

people.name: Kawennanoron
people.text: A Mohawk matron of the Wolf Clan, of the Keepers of the Eastern Door, whose longhouse stands nearest the trail from Albany, so every traveler eats her corn soup before anyone else's. She decides which guest gets which bowl, and what the council hears about each, and she wants the Albany traders to stop carrying rum up the trail before the next council. A host, and the gate into the Confederacy from the east.

people.name: Chuqui Ocllo
people.text: A brewer of Cusco whose house's *aqha* is poured at Situa and at half the *mink'a* gatherings in the valley, keeping track out loud of who owes whom a day's work, back three harvests. She has fed the Sapa Inca's officers, a captured Spanish muleteer and a huaca's keeper at one bench without anyone leaving hungry or angry, and wants her son home from the Apurímac front in time to dig his own field. A host and a contact who knows everyone in Cusco, and what they owe.

people.name: Domingas da Costa
people.text: A free woman from Angola who sells cooked food from a tray in Salvador's lower city and keeps the key to the Rosary brotherhood's chest. She bought her own freedom a coin at a time and has helped buy six others since; the seventh is in Life Here's hooks. A patron of the brotherhood's chest, who pays in food, favors and a welcome in every Black brotherhood on the coast.

regions.intro: The setting's own people here. Sehpin, Kilimoar, Lihpahnu and Tinashe Gumbo, first, are one cast on Pohnpei. Each has a pregen sheet. The sheets are on the site, perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia.

people.name: Sehpin
people.text: A yam-grower's child the basalt answered at fifteen, now one of the few left who can raise a course at Nan Madol, and the keeper of the chiefly dead behind the walls. Find them waist-deep in the shallows at dusk with a palm on a fallen column, or at the feast house the day the prize yams come in. A Nahnmwarki asks for their work and so do the samworo, and neither has it by right; Sehpin wants to stop being asked to choose. A patron or mentor: when traders off the Monsoon Road ask how the stones were raised, Sehpin tells them the truth, that you ask, and they write it down as if it were a lie (see Hooks).

people.name: Kilimoar
people.text: A *samworo*, a priest of Pohnpei, who made Sehpin listen to the basalt for a year before letting them touch it. He keeps to the old teachers' stones at Salapwuk, or goes to Nan Madol at night to lay offerings on a *pei* the chiefs have forgotten. He wants the rites kept by someone after him, and not sold, and would rather Sehpin kept them than built sea walls for a chief. A mentor or rival; when a Monsoon Road trader asked to buy the method, he laughed so long the trader left.

people.name: Lihpahnu
people.text: Sehpin's elder sister, who grows the family's prize yams for the chiefs' feasts and considers this the family's real work. She's up to her elbows in red earth above the lagoon, or at the feast house the night the yams come in on poles. She loves Sehpin, finds the stones a little showy and wants to grow a yam so large the Nahnmwarki remembers her name and not her sibling's. Anyone who wants Sehpin goes through her kitchen, and she feeds them first and asks questions after.

people.name: Tinashe Gumbo
people.text: A Mutapan Mhizha, grandson of the royal medium Ambuya Rudo Gumbo, who came out along the Monsoon Road to learn how Pohnpei's stones were raised, and whether the method can be bought. He waits at the edge of a Nahnmwarki's feast house for leave to see Nan Madol at night, his construct holding a sunshade over him while he asks every passing child the Pohnpeian word for something. He has watched Sehpin talk a column into a wall and is no longer sure what he came to buy. A rival or contact, and the trader of the stones (see Hooks).

people.name: Sarongelug
people.text: A *palu*, a master navigator of the Carolinian wayfinding schools on Polowat, who holds the star compass and the swells in his head. A Dutch captain offered him a year's silver for a passage no chart shows, and he told the captain, kindly, that the school doesn't sell and the captain couldn't pay. He wants one more voyage to Guam before the Spanish change it. A mentor or contact for a navigator for hire (see Hooks).

people.name: Asiga
people.text: A Chamorro *makåhna* in Hagåtña, a healer and speaker to the ancestors, who will watch San Vitores's mission come ashore in June, studying the black-robed men the way she'd study a new plant. Chief Kepuha has welcomed the Jesuits and she respects Kepuha; she hasn't decided whether to be the priests' best friend or their worst problem, and wants her curious daughter not to decide anything quickly. A contact or foil for the mission (see Trouble Brewing).

people.name: Tetua
people.text: A young ʻarioi of ʻOro's society from Raʻiātea, whose troupe mocks the chiefs in dance and verse and is fed handsomely for it. She can imitate a chief's walk so exactly that his own sons can't breathe, and she wants the next grade of the society, and its leg tattoos, before the troupe sails for the other islands. A contact who hears what chiefs say when they think the performers are only performing.

people.name: Kaiawa
people.text: A tohunga of a Waikato hapū who heals with the waters that run toward Hawaiki and keeps the pā's fires lit when patupaiarehe flutes sound on the ridge. She wants the flutes off her ridge for good, is ready to go up and ask what that would cost, and tells anyone who'll listen that a pause is not a peace. A mentor or ally for the flute (see Hooks).

people.name: Fusipala
people.text: A woman of a chiefly house at Lapaha on Tongatapu who keeps the order of the *ʻinasi*, the first-fruits presentation to the Tuʻi Tonga: whose yams, mats and kava go where, and what it means when a chief sends less. The Tuʻi Tonga is sacred and doesn't count things, so she counts them for him, with a knotted cord in her lap, and wants to know which chief is sending short on purpose this year. A patron who hires strangers when a canoe goes missing, because a stranger can ask what a chief can't.

people.name: Hoʻolulu
people.text: A *kahuna lāʻau lapaʻau* of Kona on Hawaiʻi Island, a healer by plants and prayer who studied twenty years before he was let near a patient, and who hurries for no one. He has treated the warriors of three rival chiefs and been thanked by all three, and wants an apprentice patient enough to learn a plant's prayer before its use. A mentor or ally; when no plant answers, he goes up the mountain and asks why.

people.name: Hinewai
people.text: The *kaikaranga* of a Waikato hapū, whose call brings every visiting party onto the marae, so hers is the first voice anyone hears on arriving. She is Kaiawa's cousin, and thinks Kaiawa should come down off the ridge and eat something. A host and an ally for a party that arrives properly.

people.name: Kalehua
people.text: A chief's daughter of Kona on Hawaiʻi Island, who has won the Makahiki surfing three years running and composes the chants that tease whoever she beats. She wants a match against someone worth beating. An ally, and the chief's daughter in the hook (see Life Here).

regions.intro: The setting's own people here. Aisulu, Kenzhe, Zhamal-apa and Gaukhar, first, share one Kazakh camp. Each has a pregen sheet. The sheets are on the site, perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia.

people.name: Aisulu
people.text: A Kazakh *batyr* of giant blood, a goliath who rides watch for her camp against Dzungar raiders and the Wild Hunt alike. Find her on a ridge of the autumn pasture at dusk, standing in her stirrups a head taller than any rider on the line, a golden eagle on her arm. On the steppe the camp's own riders ride out against the Hunt and she rides first; she hasn't told the camp that the Hunt's best rider has her brother's laugh. An ally who wants her brother Kenzhe home and himself again, and knows the second is harder.

people.name: Kenzhe
people.text: Aisulu's brother, a Kazakh rider taken by the pari three winters ago, who came back riding ahead of the Wild Hunt and takes people rather than killing them. In the dark half he waits just past a camp's watch fires, smiling his old smile and calling the watch by their childhood names. He isn't cruel: he takes people the way you'd carry a friend out of a burning yurt, and he wants to bring his sister across because he truly believes she'd be happier there. A villain or foil; the camp still sets a bowl for him at feasts, and something empties it.

people.name: Zhamal-apa
people.text: A Kazakh midwife of the same camp, a Hedge Witch who drives the albasty off birthing mothers by announcing that a hero has arrived, and pays for each healing out of her own body when there is nothing else to take it from (the Hedge Witch's way; *The Classes*, Physician). She shouts "The hero has come!" so convincingly that the hero, Aisulu, ducks into the yurt looking embarrassed. The camp's mullah calls it superstition; she says the mullah has never had a baby. A mentor or ally, who wants the camp to winter where a midwife can be reached.

people.name: Gaukhar
people.text: A Kazakh *aqyn*, a singer of improvised verse, from Aisulu's camp, whom nobody on the autumn pasture has beaten in an aitys in six years. She sings the bride out of her mother's yurt at every wedding in the valley, and she knows every family's quarrels because she has put them in verse. The camp's singer in the hook (see Life Here).

people.name: Nurbibi
people.text: A steppe gnome, the first to study the griffins' kin as animals rather than legends, nine days into a watch in a felt blind on a ridge of red sandstone; she has watched one brood its eggs on warm quartz and written "a mother" in a careful hand, with the date. Buyers in Bukhara, Moscow and London court her notebooks, and she wants the little monsters described properly before a cabinet gives them a Latin name and the wrong diet. A contact or ally, and the naturalist of the specimen hook, if the table likes.

people.name: Bibi Oysha
people.text: A Bukharan *otin*, a woman teacher, who writes the protective talismans for her father's Naqshbandi lodge and teaches the science of letters to girls the madrasas won't take. She has outlived half the scholars who said a woman couldn't do it, and wants one of her girls admitted to read in a madrasa library with the door open. A mentor or patron, and the reason the lodge's shelter holds.

people.name: Lala Sukhdev
people.text: A Multani moneylender, one of some five hundred Indian bankers in Bukhara's caravanserais, who weighs a herder's silver on a hand scale and turns the beam so the herder can read it. He'll advance a party anything against a bill on Surat, and the Bukhara buyer who wants Nurbibi's live beast writes his offers through him. He wants to go home to Multan rich enough to stay, and can't until the cousin who is to take over his clients comes, and the cousin keeps not coming. A patron or contact.

people.name: Tseren Dorji
people.text: A *zaisang*, a Dzungar noble official in the khan's tent in the Ili valley, who has watched Sengge's half-brothers count their men and wants Sengge's brother home from Tibet before they move. He needs someone to carry a letter, and an argument, to teachers in Tibet who can't be ordered, and pays in good Dzungar guns. The patron of the vow (see Hooks), who wants the monk home and the khan alive, in that order if it can't be both.

people.name: Gelong Tsereng
people.text: A Khalkha Buddhist monk of Erdene Zuu who heals the sick on the herding round and burns the shamans' *ongon* because the law says to, and has stopped arguing about what the images hold. He sets a felt ongon on the coals, then bandages the hand of the woman who made it, and keeps one he couldn't burn in a box under his bed. A foil or ally, who has asked twice for a younger monk to take over the round and been refused.

people.name: Iliqa
people.text: An Evenki shaman of the upper Lena, chosen by a dead shaman's spirit through an illness that lasted three winters, who walks the Tree's three worlds for her clan. On tribute day she is at the Yakutsk fort's gate, asking to see the hostage house, where her nephew is held; the fort wants fur, and she gives exactly as many sables as the forest can spare, which is never enough. An ally or mentor for the hostage (see Hooks).

people.name: Avdotya Shchukina
people.text: A Cossack widow who runs a sable-smuggling family from the back room of her late husband's tavern below the Tobolsk kremlin, pouring kvass for a governor's clerk with one hand and sliding him a pelt with her foot. She buys furs from both sides and lights a candle for every runner she has lost. A villain or contact, who wants her youngest son out of the trade and a long way from Tobolsk, and will pay a party to take him.

people.name: Avetik of Julfa
people.text: A New Julfa merchant's younger son sent to Astrakhan to learn the silk trade, who learned nard, the Persian backgammon, instead and wins more from Kalmyk princes than his father makes on silk. He keeps a board in the Armenian merchants' yard in Astrakhan and plays in the Kalmyk camps across the Volga in summer, and he wants enough winnings to buy a ship of his own before his father stops writing. Comic relief or a rival; his father's letters get shorter every season.

people.name: Sardaana
people.text: A Sakha singer of the Lena meadows who leads the osuokhai at Ysyakh, and has kept a circle dancing from dusk to the next noon. She pays her family's fur tribute and resents every pelt, and wants this year's circle large enough for the fort to hear. A host and a contact on the Lena, and the bride's cousin on tribute day (see Life Here).

blocks.text: **Real people act as history records.** Mariana of Austria, Colbert, the Kangxi Emperor, Aurangzeb, Mukombwe: they're where the record puts them, doing what it says they did, and the party can be in the room. Three rules keep that honest. Give no real person invented words: describe what they decide, and let the record's own documents speak when you need a voice. An act history doesn't record (the Archbishop of Toledo leading an escort through Spain's gate) is the setting's call; know when you've made one. And keep the record's shape: the party can delay a confessor's fall, but nobody changes who was king. A real person makes a splendid patron, judge or obstacle, and a poor villain.

**The setting's own people** are the characters the book invents: the four on the book's cover, and Shiri, the Sharper and the Wit, and Gottlieb von Schleich, who have entries below. Give each a scene and keep the speeches short. At home a table may play anyone, these included; the reservation in the Contributors and License appendix governs publishing, not play.

items: **Simbarashe Moyo**, Mutapa's great artificer (entry below).

**Ilyanor Sael**, Lanternhall's elf: one of the high Hidden holding a shape in a Basel teaching hospital, who crossed with something of the Hidden still in the soul, and so remembers. A teacher, a licensing problem for every Church and a reason for a Physician party to exist. *Hooks:* a Lanternhall graduate hanged at Lyon left a letter saying Ilyanor taught her everything she did; a canon of Basel's cathedral wants proof that the Chair of Vital Studies remembers being Hidden, and has hired someone to get it.

**Anselme Lafrenaye**, the Gamester of the French court, a graying French halfling with his own chair at the king's high play at Saint-Germain, and at Versailles when the king takes the court to his pleasure house there. He knows the odds on everything and a few of the corridors anyway. A Counsellor's patron, rival or model. *Hooks:* he wants the man who beat him at a hand he couldn't lose found and brought to the table again; a general who lost a dispatch to him at lansquenet wants it won back before the king hears it was staked.
**Simon Horowitz**, the Kabbalist of Venice's ghetto and the Venice Job's contact (entry below).

blocks.text: Simbarashe Moyo

A Mhizha, about eighty, and the great artificer: the man who showed that lightning is electricity, that electricity is its own force and that lightning is the purest form magical force takes in matter. Everything Mutapa makes runs on something he found. A table that wants to play him has his sheet among the pregens on the site (perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia).

He was a smith's son from the plateau, of the Moyo clan, whose totem is the heart. In his twenties he watched the first masters on the Dyke die of the sorting; in the 1630s he built a rod to call the lightning down safely, turned it sideways into the first Arc Gun, then turned his lightning into the forge that made platinum a metal (The State of the World, Mutapa and the Indian Ocean, The Metal of White Fire). Then he noticed that the metal which makes one lamp behave like the next would make a piece of the Hidden behave at all, and he began building rooms inside the Hidden, one at a time, for the crafters who would come after him (Possible Futures, Basa Remhizha, below).

He has lost twice. The first time was to his own apprentice, Nyarai Soko, who wrote down how he did things so that anyone with the hands could learn them; that is the guild, and he has never quite forgiven it. The second time was to the court, which began selling his work abroad and sending his shewstones to every crowned head in the world. He fought both and lost both, and he still turns up to argue.

He lives in Sofala's old town, in the workshop he took when the city was taken, and goes to court as little as the king allows. The iron construct is at the door before anyone knocks. He wears a work coat with too many pockets and a burn on the left cuff he won't have mended. He works every day, on small things: the songs the guild's singing birds sing, a pair of speaking wires he would rather the world had than the shewstones, a better pump. He is courteous, quick and funny, and has no patience for flattery. He asks visitors to explain something simple, a lamp, a hinge, why a kettle sings, and listens to how they do it.

He writes letters. Every year a few go out in his own hand to people abroad who have opened a curiosity and closed it again, or asked a good question in a coffeehouse where a Mutapan factor was listening. Some of them answer. The guild reads the ones it catches, and the spymaster reads the ones the guild misses.

**His choice.** He has asked the court for passage abroad and hasn't said why. The book doesn't say what he chooses or when; it is the fifth turning point in Possible Futures, and it belongs to the table. By default he stays and keeps fighting at court until something forces his hand; the hooks below are the somethings. It can take many shapes: he stays and keeps fighting at court; he sails and gives the lightning to the world's natural philosophers as a science anyone can learn, which by his own rule it is; or he goes into the Hidden and closes the door behind him. Whichever it is, someone will try to stop him. The Shava house has already sent men to his workshop at night, the spymaster keeps a file on him, and the guild would rather he stayed where it can see him.

**At the table.** He gives a party a scene. As a mentor he asks more than he answers, and what he teaches stays taught. As a patron he is the most dangerous commission in the setting: he pays in a retuned curiosity, a letter to the guild with his name on it, or an honest answer, and he has built no weapon for anyone since the first Arc Gun. To a crown's crew he is the prize every ministry in Europe would most like to bring home.
Hooks

items: A letter in the great artificer's hand reaches a party member abroad, answering a question they asked a Mutapan lamp-tuner in passing a year ago. It invites them to Sofala. The guild has a copy.
His construct has walked out of the workshop at night and is standing at the guild hall's door. Nobody sent it, and it won't move.
The Shava house's men came back, and this time they took his notebook from the 1630s. He wants it back before the court learns it was ever gone.
He wants passage on the party's ship, under another name, as far as Surat. He won't say where he goes after that.

blocks.text: Shiri

A Counsellor (Spymaster), about forty-five, and Mutapa's foreign intelligence. Her agents call her Shiri, "bird" in Shona, after the soapstone bird on her seal, and she has never corrected them. Her own name is in the ledgers of the House of the Bird, Mutapa's bank, and nowhere else.

She grew up at the fair at Dambarare, a customs officer's daughter, and by twelve spoke Shona, Swahili, Portuguese and enough Gujarati to know what a trader said when he thought no one at the scales could follow. As a clerk of correspondents' letters at the House of the Bird she noticed that the Bird's correspondents, read together, say what every court is about to do: who is borrowing for a fleet, who has stopped paying, who is buying platinum and at what price. The Bird made her its reader, and when the court began selling abroad, its reader became its spymaster.

She runs the thinnest service in the world from one room above the bank, with one window, a table and a bench. Her assets are a handful of factors in the ports, the Bird's correspondents, and a few Mhizha abroad who retune curiosities in great houses and write home about what they see. She has never met most of them. Every report is answered by the next ship, even if the answer is one line, and every agent is paid on time, every time.
She belongs to the Spymaster's Club, as every court's spymaster does, the only member whose king makes the stones. The others assume she can hear through the shewstones; she lets them assume it.

In 1668 she is watching four things: the London artificer and his English apprentice; who told Spain what its platina was; the shewstone push, which she and the great artificer are the two to see clearly; and above all the gate at Toledo and the warded blank, which she means to understand before Europe acts. She and Simbarashe Moyo agree about the stones and about little else. His choice is the thing she most fears and can least prevent, and she has a file on him as thick as any court's.

**At the table.** A party meets her factor first, and gets its orders by letter under the bird seal; a crew that does three jobs well is asked up the stairs, once, to the bench in the room above the bank. As a patron she pays in gold by the *mithqal* and in credit on the Bird, and never asks a party to do what it can't. As an opponent she seldom kills. She ruins credit: a factor stops honoring your paper, and a European crew discovers that nobody in any port will lend to it. On the fair's rest day she plays tsoro in the market at Sofala with whoever sits down, and loses on purpose to children.
Hooks

items: Her factor in Venice has stopped answering. She wants to know whether he is dead, turned or in love, and she wants the answer before the Sensa.
A Mutapan factor in Lisbon has been seen going in at the Holy Office's side door. She wants him followed for a week, and stopped only if he goes in a second time.
One of her Mhizha abroad has started writing home in a cipher she never gave him.
She wants to know who is paying for the great artificer's passage. She doesn't say what she will do with the answer.

blocks.text: Simon Horowitz
A Warlock (Envoy), about thirty-five, and the Kabbalist of Venice's ghetto. He is the Venice Job's contact.

He is a Horowitz of Prague, of the Levite family that built a synagogue there; his grandfather brought the household to Venice, and he lives on the fourth floor above a German congregation's synagogue door. He earns his living by reading: contracts, old deeds and, for the Council of Ten, any hand their own clerks can't make out. The Republic locks the ghetto's gates from sunset to dawn, so he works at night, by a candle-end.

Two years ago much of the ghetto believed Sabbatai Zevi was the messiah, and some families sold their leases and furniture to be ready. Then Sabbatai Zevi took the turban before the sultan. Simon hadn't believed, and being right didn't make him kinder: he trusts no one who promises anything. In March 1668 the messiah's prophet, Nathan of Gaza, lands at Venice, and the rabbis and the city make him sign that his prophecies were his own imagination. Simon is asked to read the hand of the confession.

**The book.** An angel gave Simon a book and told him to read it. By default the angel is Raziel, the keeper of secrets, who in Kabbalist tradition gave a book to the first man; that is why the gift came as a book. Simon can read the script and can't yet read the language. Each page gives way after weeks of work, and each page he reads is something he can then do, which is how he comes by an Envoy's powers (*The Classes*, Warlock, Envoy). He is eleven pages in. What the book is for belongs to the table; by default it is the book Raziel gave the first man, and its last page opens a door the angel wants opened.

**The golem.** By default the ghetto's golem followed its word from Prague to Venice: Simon's grandfather knew the word that stops it. The burial society knows the word now, and so does Simon. The golem itself is in Adventures and Hooks, The Venice Job.

**At the table.** Simon is young, sleepless and sharp-tongued. He is a contact first: he reads what nobody else can, he knows how the Ten lock their rooms and he can walk a party past the golem. As a teacher he takes an Envoy or a Wizard who will work, and he asks to be paid in texts: a copied page, a borrowed manuscript, a letter carried to Prague or Amsterdam and the answer brought back. As a patron he hires for whatever he can't do from behind locked gates. A party that says plainly what it wants from him, and what it will take, gets further than one that flatters or promises.
Hooks

items: The twelfth page names a house in Venice outside the ghetto, and Simon can't go there after dark. He wants someone to go, and to tell him exactly what is over the door.
The Ten send him a letter to read. It is in his own hand, and he never wrote it.
The golem has started stopping at Simon's door each night and waiting. It last did that the week his grandfather died.

Nathan of Gaza is being sent on to Livorno under escort. One family in the ghetto wants him to slip the escort, the rabbis want him delivered, and Simon wants ten minutes with him first, to ask what he saw.

blocks.text: The Sharper and the Wit

A Gamester and a Courtier who work as a pair: English, in their twenties, banned from more houses than most people have visited, very funny about the English and much better brought up than they let on. They're written as player characters a table can take as they are, or meet as rivals across a gaming table.

**Kit Harrow**, Counsellor (Gamester), 24. A Cavalier baronet's daughter whose father came home with the king in 1660 and lost the estate at hazard at the Groom Porter's inside two years. Kit learned the game to win it back, and found she was better at it than anyone she'd ever met. She plays in breeches, does the season like a campaign (Whitehall in the winter, Tunbridge Wells in summer, Paris when London gets too hot) and keeps a pocketbook of every debt anyone owes her. Two earls and a bishop owe her money. She owes it to one moneylender in Lombard Street, who is very patient, and very frightening.

**Ned Ashcombe**, Courtier (College of Verse), 26. The younger son of a Royalist colonel killed at Worcester, raised on a promise the Restoration hasn't kept. His lampoons are portraits of types that all London sings, and everyone is sure the next verse is about the man beside them; one got him banished from court for a season. He fences well and insists he doesn't, and has fought five duels and lost none, mostly because he made his opponents laugh.

**The couple.** They met across a hazard table, where Ned tried to cheat her and Kit let him, to see how good he was, and they were married a year later in the Fleet, on a bet Kit won. Ned maintains it doesn't count and has never once tried to prove it. They fight in public, in verse and in arithmetic; nobody has ever seen either of them take a side against the other.

**The act.** Kit plays, and Ned works the room. A couplet in his mouth is a signal to her (a rhyme on the king means the bank is weak; a line of Donne means the man on her left is cheating), and nobody in Europe listens to Ned closely enough to notice. When the house turns ugly, she counts, he ripostes and they leave by the window. They're banned from the Groom Porter's for a season, the Duke of York's apartments for a lampoon and two Paris *académies de jeu* for winning; Venice's Ridotto still lets them in, masked like everyone else.
**At the table.**

items: *As player characters,* both are 8th level, and their sheets are on the site (perceptualmechanics.com/euphonia). They're the pair for an intrigue game: Kit's Everyone's a Mark finds the tell, and Ned's Read finds who holds the power. In a fight, Kit's Big Player puts Ned where he needs to be, and her Know the Odds tells him exactly how much is left to cut.

*As NPCs,* they're the party's best friends or its worst rivals at any table in Europe (cross one of them and you've crossed both), and the people every Spymaster's Club agent would like to recruit, since no one notices who they talk to.
*As a team,* every debt is a hook.

blocks.text: Hooks

items: Kit has won a sealed dispatch case at ombre from a drunk envoy, and has no idea what is in it. Someone does, and is already at her lodging.
Ned's latest lampoon names no one, and everyone at court thinks it's about them. A duke wants the author's name; the author wants the party to find out which duke.
The patient moneylender in Lombard Street has finally called Kit's debt, and he doesn't want money. He wants her to lose one game, on purpose, at the Ridotto, to a man who has never lost.

A rival offers Ned a place at court, a pension and a wife with an estate, if he'll swear the Fleet marriage was a joke. He's asked the party to find out who's paying for the offer, and he hasn't told Kit.

blocks.text: Gottlieb von Schleich

A Counsellor (Spymaster) and Wizard, about fifty, and the man nobody invites. He's a Freiherr from a corner of Franconia, and envoy to the Perpetual Diet at Regensburg for an imperial county so small that it shares one vote with a whole bench of counts. The Diet opened in 1663 and never closed, so Schleich has had five years with nothing to do, and he has filled them by going everywhere.

He is at every reception in Regensburg and Vienna, every wedding, every lying-in-state, every opera and every hunt, at the edge of every conversation that matters, holding a glass he never drinks. Three courts have licensed him as a wizard, because none of them could find a reason not to. He's damp, attentive and agreeable; he laughs a moment after everyone else; he remembers your mother's name and your debts. He writes it all down in a small green book. He is never quite rude enough to be shown the door, and he always knows which door you came in by.

**At the table.** The party meets him in every city, and he has always heard. He offers help nobody asked for, and it's always good. The table's slow discovery is that he is never wrong, and that somebody is paying for the green book: his county can't afford his coat.
Hooks

items: Schleich greets the party by name in a city they arrived in that morning, and congratulates them on a job they haven't taken yet.
The green book has been stolen. Half of Vienna is relieved; the other half has started to worry about who has it now. Schleich asks the party to get it back, and to not read it.
Someone has finally poisoned Schleich, not fatally, and he wants to know who. He has a list, and it's long.
A minister offers the party a fortune to find out who Schleich reports to. The first clue is a bill for the coat.
